reviewScope: Six independently worded state/restricted-stack contracts, thirty actual algorithm bodies, state/error ordering, identity observations, independent transcript models, correctness arguments, worked traces and complexity bounds. Execution counts are recorded separately and do not imply live integration.

questions.algorithm: Three disjoint fixed array intervals with separate sizes.
questions.review: Each language uses one payload array of length three times capacity and three counters. Bounds are checked before payload access, then full/empty checks before mutation. Stack slots cannot be borrowed. Fixed capacity is explicit rather than silently substituting the flexible-stack variant. Capacity multiplication is safe within 1..256.

questions.algorithm: A linked entry records its value and the minimum of its entire prefix.
questions.review: Every language restores repeated minima by exposing the previous entry. Integer endpoints remain valid payloads; empty accesses throw the stated error rather than using a sentinel. There is no hidden scan or growable minimum array. Constant-time operation claims explicitly separate allocation and destruction/garbage collection.

questions.algorithm: Growable arrays of capacity-limited stacks; PopAt propagates each following bottom value into the preceding gap.
questions.review: The specification chooses rollover and compacted indices explicitly. All five implementations remove exactly the selected segment top, retain other values in logical order and remove only an empty final stack. Bounds precede writes. The independent oracle removes from one flat logical array instead of duplicating the rollover algorithm.
questions.complexity: Push/Pop amortized constant time; PopAt O(s*capacity), reflecting actual array-front shifts rather than claiming constant time per affected stack.

questions.algorithm: Two payload stacks, transferring input only when output is empty.
questions.review: C#/Java stack wrappers, C++ vector ends, Python list ends and JavaScript array ends all obey the stack-only payload restriction. New additions stay behind existing output values. Size uses the two stored counts. Each element transfers at most once, justifying amortized rather than worst-case constant Remove/Peek.

questions.algorithm: Insertion into one auxiliary stack, moving larger tops back to the input before each insertion, then reversing into the original stack.
questions.review: All five mutate the supplied IntStack and use only its public stack operations, one auxiliary IntStack and scalar temporaries. Strict greater-than preserves duplicates and prevents equal-value shuttling. The final top is smallest, and the adapter observes ascending repeated pops. Worst-case quadratic time and linear auxiliary space match the actual algorithm.

questions.algorithm: Two linked species queues with increasing admission numbers; compare heads for unrestricted adoption.
questions.review: Every language stores and returns the supplied Animal object, not its Id or a clone. Ids are unique arbitrary labels and do not establish age. Invalid species is checked before queue/counter writes. Empty categories return null. Tail clearing allows subsequent enqueue after a species becomes empty. Actual copied-animal submissions were executed and rejected in all five languages.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Nullable linked-entry accesses follow checks; built-in int storage covers the full signed 32-bit payload domain. Animal identity observation uses ReferenceEquals, and reflection unwraps only the documented BankError while other failures remain failures.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Integer payloads and at most 2001 operations stay within exact Number arithmetic. End-only array operations implement the restricted queue; front shifting is confined to the explicitly nonconstant PopAt. Animal returns use strict object identity, and readonly model fields are frozen.
languageBindingReview.python: Node records preserve references with is-based Animal observation rather than overloaded equality. Exact bool/int checks reject Python's bool-as-int subtype ambiguity. The queue uses list ends only; PopAt explicitly uses pop(0) with its stated shifting cost.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Caller-owned Animal pointers are never deleted by the solution. Queue/stack entries use unique_ptr ownership; removal first moves the owning entry into a local before moving its Next, avoiding assignment through a destroyed owning subobject. Restricted SortStack receives the input by reference. Counters cannot overflow within the transcript bound.
languageBindingReview.java: ArrayDeque<Integer> supplies stack-end operations; automatic unboxing returns primitive int values, not reference comparisons. Species checks use String.equals. Animal observation uses IdentityHashMap. Linked entries are static nested classes and retain original Animal references.
